roster.name: SED-ML (Simulation Experiment Description Markup Language)
roster.description: An XML-based standard for encoding simulation experiments and reports (including sedml:report); the BioSimulations docs include conventions for encoding experiments, targets, algorithm parameters, and report structures.

roster.name: COMBINE/OMEX archive format
roster.description: The standard archive format for bundling models, SED-ML files, metadata, and results into a single OMEX file; the site documents conventions for organizing archives and where outputs/logs/reports should be placed.

roster.name: OMEX Metadata (RDF-XML)
roster.description: An RDF-XML metadata format/recommendation for annotating meaning, provenance, and credibility of COMBINE/OMEX simulation projects; the docs give specific predicates/objects to use and recommend this format for project metadata.

roster.name: BioSimulators tool specification (biosimulators.json)
roster.description: A JSON schema/format for describing the specifications of simulation tools (supported frameworks, algorithms, parameters, interfaces, citations, container image metadata) used by the BioSimulators registry; provided in the template and documentation as the required tool metadata format.

roster.name: BioSimulators execution log format for COMBINE/OMEX
roster.description: A BioSimulators-defined format for recording the execution status and outcomes of simulation projects (per-SED-ML document/task/output statuses, stdout/stderr, reasons for failure) packaged within COMBINE/OMEX archives.

roster.name: KISAO (Kinetic Simulation Algorithm Ontology)
roster.description: An ontology for identifying and annotating simulation algorithms and algorithm parameters (KISAO IDs); the materials show use of KISAO identifiers to specify algorithms/parameters in tool and SED-ML descriptions.

roster.name: HDF5 report format for SED-ML reports
roster.description: A convention (used by BioSimulations) for serializing sedml:report outputs into HDF5 files with defined table shapes and paths so tools produce consistent report files for visualization and reuse.
